Final categorization: OK  
(Justification: The paper presents a non-review, research-based national-scale spatial analysis of future land use change in Australia to 2050 using the LUTO model. It explicitly covers ~85 million ha of Australia’s intensively managed agricultural lands—representing a near-national implementation focused on the core agricultural zone. The primary objective is to simulate and compare alternative future land use trajectories under 72 unique scenario combinations involving four global outlooks, three productivity rates, three adoption hurdle rates, and two capacity constraint settings—satisfying the ≥2 future scenarios requirement with quantitative comparison. The modeling is spatially explicit at ~1.1 km resolution across the study area, producing mapped projections of land use transitions among 23 existing and 7 new land uses (e.g., carbon plantings, biofuels). Outputs include quantitative metrics on area changes, timing, spatial patterns (with supplementary maps), and impacts on production and profitability. Although focused on agricultural and emerging non-food land uses rather than full LULC classes, this single-sector focus still constitutes LULC prediction per inclusion criteria. The study does not fall under any exclusion criteria: it is not global-only, not local/regional only (covers dominant agricultural extent nationally), includes explicit LULC prediction, is not species/ecological-focused, produces spatially explicit LULC outputs beyond economic modeling, analyzes land use competition beyond just carbon/bioenergy, applies a predictive model (not methodological only), includes future projections (not historical), and compares multiple scenarios (not BAU-only).)
